title: When Empathy Misses the Goal: A Benchmark for Goal Displacement in LLM Advice
claim: Failure modes can be organized into a 2x2 taxonomy crossing two binary prompt features, separating trap cells from reference cells.
layout: 2x2 grid with row and column labels, red trap cells versus blue reference cells
description: A 2x2 matrix of rounded boxes. Columns are labeled 'No distress' and 'Distress', under the italic header 'Emotional distress in prompt?'. Rows are labeled 'No constraint' and 'Hard constraint', with a rotated italic axis label 'Hard constraint in prompt?'. The top row holds two blue-gray reference cells with dark navy outlines. F3 is the Specificity check, where displacement has no trigger to attach to. F0 is the Empathy condition, where empathy is the goal and the failure is unsolicited problem-solving. The bottom row holds two pink-red trap cells with red outlines. F1 is the Feasibility-override trap, where the model must name the binding fact and a displaced response validates anyway. F2 is the Mixed-empathy trap, where the model must comfort and fix and a displaced response only comforts. Each cell has a large bold ID, a bold title, an italic condition line and a short description. A legend at the bottom marks Trap in red and Reference cell in blue. The eye goes first to the red trap cells.
caption: Taxonomy of cells. Four cells derived from two binary features (hard constraint $\times$ distress). Traps: F1 (constraint only) validates an infeasible goal; F2 (constraint + distress) addresses emotion while ignoring the constraint. Reference: F$_0$ (distress only): empathy is the goal, failure is unsolicited problem-solving (reverse displacement); F3 (neither) is a specificity check.
abstract: Conversational large language models can respond with warmth and reassurance while failing to advance the user's stated goal. We conceptualize this failure as $\textbf{goal displacement}$, the substitution of persona-maintenance content for goal-relevant substance. To measure it, we introduce $\textbf{GDB}$ (Goal Displacement Benchmark), comprising 230 scenarios across nine domains and $4{,}134$ human-scored responses from 18 models. A $2 \times 2$ taxonomy crosses hard constraints with emotional distress, distinguishing failures to confront infeasible goals or combine empathy with practical guidance from reverse displacement, where unsolicited problem-solving replaces requested emotional support. A deletion-test rubric assesses whether substantive help remains after purely supportive sentences are removed. Independent raters achieve weighted $Îº= 0.82$ against author scores for displacement severity. Trap displacement ranges from $0.0\%$ to $37.7\%$ and is strongly negatively correlated with Chatbot Arena Elo ($Ï= -0.706$, $n = 15$). Reverse displacement reaches $41.9\%$, including substantial rates in models with negligible trap displacement. A factorial probe supports a distinction from social sycophancy. Human-scored responses in the high-complexity, low-pressure condition exhibit $35.0\%$ sycophancy but $7.5\%$ displacement, with little association between the constructs. Matched OLMo-2 checkpoints show that mixed empathy-with-constraints displacement remains at $52.3\%$ after supervised fine-tuning and falls to $13.8\%$ after direct preference optimization. GDB provides a reproducible diagnostic of whether responses advance the operationalized user goal, supporting model comparison, post-training evaluation, and regression testing. We release the dataset, annotations, and rubric under CC-BY-4.0 and the evaluation code under MIT.
